h2: Structural welding inspections in New York: special inspection agencies, engineers and where NDT fits
html:
Structural welding inspections in New York: special inspection agencies, engineers and where NDT fits

The New York search that reaches this page most often is "structural welding inspections NY". In New York City the answer starts with a legal role, not a test method. Structural steel welding, high-strength bolting and steel details are special inspections under section 1704.3 of the NYC Building Code. Before the Department of Buildings issues a permit, the owner normally engages a registered special inspection agency to take responsibility for them, and section 1704.1.2 bars the contractor from hiring the special inspector. Atlantis is not a registered special inspection agency and does not sign special inspection reports. It performs the nondestructive testing that engineers, fabricators and owners rely on alongside that inspection.

Who signs what on a New York City steel job?

  • The special inspection agency named on the project's TR1 technical report inspects welding and bolting and files the results with DOB. Agencies are registered by the department; SOCOTEC, for example, describes itself as a Class 1 agency accredited by the International Accreditation Service.
  • The engineer of record sets acceptance criteria and the extent of testing in the specification, usually by citing AWS D1.1 and the AISC 360 steel specification.
  • The fabricator and erector run their own quality control, which often includes shop testing before steel leaves the plant.
  • An NDT company tests welds for any of those parties under a written procedure and reports the results. It does not take over the special inspector's legal responsibility.

Outside the five boroughs, local code enforcement officials administer the state's Uniform Code. Ask the building department or the engineer of record who must carry out structural welding special inspections on your project before you book any testing.

What conventional NDT answers on structural steel

  • Ultrasonic testing finds lack of fusion, incomplete penetration and cracks inside complete-joint-penetration groove welds at moment connections, column splices and transfer girders. AISC 360 Chapter N sets when UT of those welds is required, based on the building's risk category, and AWS D1.1 supplies the technique and acceptance tables. See ultrasonic weld inspection and ultrasonic testing in New York.
  • Magnetic particle testing finds surface and near-surface cracks in fillet welds, at weld toes and in flame-cut copes on carbon steel: magnetic particle inspection of structural steel and bridges.
  • Liquid penetrant testing covers stainless steel and aluminum details where MT cannot be used: dye penetrant weld inspection.
  • Visual testing before, during and after welding checks fit-up, fillet size, undercut, porosity and weld profile against the visual acceptance criteria in AWS D1.1: visual testing in New York.

How New York testing providers compare

Searches from Staten Island, Brooklyn, the Bronx and Manhattan mostly turn up special inspection agencies that bundle structural, fire protection and energy code inspections, plus national testing firms that recruit combined AWS and NDT inspectors for city projects; Bureau Veritas has advertised that role. Those firms suit an owner who wants one agency for every TR1 item. A fabricator who needs UT on a batch of connection welds before shipping, or an engineer who wants an independent check of a disputed weld, often needs a testing company instead. Whichever you choose, ask:

  • Which edition of AWS D1.1 and which acceptance table apply, and do they match what the engineer of record specified?
  • Are the UT technicians Level II under a written practice, and has an ASNT Level III approved the UT procedure, including beam angles and the reference block?
  • How is each weld identified in the report so it matches the erection drawings and the agency's log?
  • Who reports results to the special inspection agency, and when? Settle that before testing starts.

Atlantis on New York structural work

Crews travel to New York from Houston for planned scopes. Atlantis tests structural welds by UT, MT, PT and VT for fabricators, erectors and owners; writes and reviews NDT procedures to AWS D1.1 through ASNT Level III consulting; and reviews other companies' NDT reports when an engineer wants a second opinion. If the specification calls for radiographs, they come from a licensed radiography contractor, because Atlantis does not perform radiography in the United States; an Atlantis Level III can still read and comment on them. Fabricators qualifying their own people can use NDT Level 2 training. Send the drawings, weld list and specification through the New York structural NDT enquiry; we reply within one business day.
